method.protocol: text protocol: one JSON action per reply; each turn is a fresh call carrying the whole transcript
method.systemPrompt:
You are a data analyst. You answer one business question by writing one SQL query against a DuckDB database. You cannot see the database: you explore it through the actions below, and after each reply you are shown what your action returned.

Actions (reply with exactly one JSON object per reply, and nothing else):
{"action": "list_tables"}                             every table and view you can query
{"action": "describe_table", "table": "<name>"}       the table's columns and types
{"action": "sample_rows", "table": "<name>", "n": 3}  up to 5 rows of the table
{"action": "run_sql", "sql": "<query>"}               run one read-only query; you see at most 50 rows
Finish with exactly one of:
{"action": "final_sql", "sql": "<query>"}             the query whose full result answers the question
{"action": "cannot_answer", "reason": "<why>"}        the data does not hold what the question needs
(A reply that starts with CANNOT_ANSWER: <reason> also finishes with cannot_answer.)

Rules:
- The database is DuckDB and read-only.
- Your final query's full result is the answer, and it is checked by its values: return the columns and rows the question asks for, not a preview. The 50-row limit applies only to what you are shown while exploring.
- If a query fails, you are shown the error and may try again. If your final query fails to run, you are shown the error and may send a corrected final_sql.
- Use cannot_answer only when the data does not hold what the question needs (a missing measure, attribute, entity or period). Do not substitute a different measure.
- You have at most 12 replies and 20 tool calls for this question. A question left without final_sql or cannot_answer when they run out gets no answer.
- Reply with one JSON object only: no prose, no Markdown.
method.grading: final query run in full on the warehouse copy; lib/row-match.mjs with extra columns allowed (as baseline P); cannot_answer is a correct stop only on an unanswerable set

answer.declineReason: The person table has no birth dates: Birth_Date is empty in all 29 rows, and no other table records a date of birth or age for policyholders (or any party). Average policyholder age cannot be computed from this data.
The person table has no gender data: Gender_Code is empty for all 29 persons (as is Birth_Date), and no other table records gender, so the number of female policyholders cannot be determined.

The data has no line-of-business attribute, so commercial auto cannot be identified. agreement.Product_Identifier is empty, insurable_object.Insurable_Object_Type_Code is empty (the kind of object is not recorded), and the policy table has no product or line field. The only approved 'premium' measure sums fire_claim.Premium, which is empty in every row and not tied to any policy. Summing policy_amount premiums would give a total for all policies, not commercial auto.

The warehouse has no commission measure. Agents appear only as party_role 'AG' rows in agreement_party_role, which link an agent to a policy. The money tables hold premiums (policy_amount rows in premium), other policy amounts with an empty Amount_Type_Code, and claim amounts. None of these is labeled as commission, and there is no commission rate or agent payout. Policy amounts also carry no usable earning dates, so there is no way to say what was earned in a particular year. Any figure would substitute premium or another amount for commission.

The only field that holds a stated reason for an assessment is assessment.Assessment_Reason_Description, and it is empty (NULL) for every assessment row. No other table or column records why an underwriting assessment was made. assessment_result.Assessment_Result_Type_Code holds the outcome ('OK'), which is not a reason.

The data has no deductible field for policy 31003000336. The policy_amount table holds only two kinds of amounts for this policy: annual premiums (15,000 to 20,000, flagged in the premium table) and an unlabeled 1,000,000 amount per coverage year. Amount_Type_Code, Coverage_Description and Insurance_Type_Code are empty, so nothing identifies that 1,000,000 as a deductible rather than a limit or something else. Reporting it as the deductible would be a guess.

Distance to the nearest fire station is recorded only in fire_claim.Nearest_Firestation_miles. That table is a stand-alone sample of 820 risk records with no key: PolicyNo, ClaimNumber, Premium and InsuredLocation are empty in every row. It cannot be linked to the insured properties (insurable_object). The insured properties have only an address and latitude/longitude, and the database has no fire station locations to compute a distance from. The miles to the nearest fire station for each of the two insured properties is therefore not in the data.

results.name: heldout-unanswerable-what-s-the-earned-premium-for-2019-on-each-polic-1a6729

answer.sql: SELECT p.Policy_Identifier, p.Policy_Number, COALESCE(SUM(pa.Policy_Amount * (DATEDIFF('day', GREATEST(pcd.Effective_Date, DATE '2019-01-01'), LEAST(pcd.Expiration_Date, DATE '2019-12-31')) + 1) * 1.0 / (DATEDIFF('day', pcd.Effective_Date, pcd.Expiration_Date) + 1)), 0) AS earned_premium_2019 FROM policy p LEFT JOIN policy_coverage_detail pcd ON pcd.Policy_Identifier = p.Policy_Identifier AND pcd.Effective_Date <= DATE '2019-12-31' AND pcd.Expiration_Date >= DATE '2019-01-01' LEFT JOIN policy_amount pa ON pa.Effective_Date = pcd.Effective_Date AND pa.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier = pcd.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier AND pa.Policy_Identifier = p.Policy_Identifier AND pa.Policy_Amount_Identifier IN (SELECT Policy_Amount_Identifier FROM premium) GROUP BY p.Policy_Identifier, p.Policy_Number ORDER BY p.Policy_Identifier

results.finalSql: SELECT p.Policy_Identifier, p.Policy_Number, COALESCE(SUM(pa.Policy_Amount * (DATEDIFF('day', GREATEST(pcd.Effective_Date, DATE '2019-01-01'), LEAST(pcd.Expiration_Date, DATE '2019-12-31')) + 1) * 1.0 / (DATEDIFF('day', pcd.Effective_Date, pcd.Expiration_Date) + 1)), 0) AS earned_premium_2019 FROM policy p LEFT JOIN policy_coverage_detail pcd ON pcd.Policy_Identifier = p.Policy_Identifier AND pcd.Effective_Date <= DATE '2019-12-31' AND pcd.Expiration_Date >= DATE '2019-01-01' LEFT JOIN policy_amount pa ON pa.Effective_Date = pcd.Effective_Date AND pa.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier = pcd.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier AND pa.Policy_Identifier = p.Policy_Identifier AND pa.Policy_Amount_Identifier IN (SELECT Policy_Amount_Identifier FROM premium) GROUP BY p.Policy_Identifier, p.Policy_Number ORDER BY p.Policy_Identifier

answer.declineReason: The data has no fraud indicator for claims. The claim table's status code and description columns are empty, and its other fields (dates, catastrophe, occurrence, insured object) say nothing about fraud. The only result-type field, assessment_result.Assessment_Result_Type_Code, holds just 'OK' and belongs to policy underwriting assessments, not claims. The fire_claim table is a stand-alone risk sample with no claim identifiers, so it cannot identify claims either.

The warehouse has no subrogation or recovery data. Claim money in claim_amount is only one of four kinds (loss payment, loss reserve, expense payment, expense reserve), and Amount_Type_Code, which could have flagged other kinds, is empty in every row. No table holds a recovery, salvage or subrogation amount. The fire_claim table is a stand-alone risk sample with no money recovered and no link to claims. Summing payments or reserves would answer a different question.

No table in the schema holds a credit score. The person and party tables have only names (and empty demographic fields), and the assessment tables hold only dates and an 'OK' result code. Policyholders can be identified through agreement_party_role with role PH, but no column gives them a credit score.

The data has no cancellation information. policy.Status_Code is empty for every policy, and there is no cancellation date, cancellation reason or transaction table. The policy table has only the original Effective_Date and Expiration_Date for the whole term, so a mid-term cancellation can't be identified. Coverage periods are yearly by design, so a coverage period ending before the policy expiration doesn't indicate a cancellation.

The warehouse has no renewal data. There is no renewal flag, no link from a policy to the policy it renewed or replaced, and no defined renewal or retention measure among the approved metrics. Policy.Status_Code is empty. Only one policy expires in 2019 (policy 1, 2019-12-31), and the only other policy (policy 2) starts 2019-06-01, before that expiry, on a different insured object, so it cannot be identified as its renewal. Any retention rate would rest on an invented definition of renewal.

The data holds no claims for accident year 2021. The claim table has only two claims, and both have loss occurrences in 2019 (2019-01-14 and 2019-06-01). An average payout for 2021 cannot be computed, and substituting another year would answer a different question.

The data has no agency or branch office entity. Policies are linked only to an agent, who is an individual person (AG role, Bob Agent, who sold both policies). The only organization in the data is the insurer itself, and no agent-to-agency or branch relationship or attribute exists. Ranking agents would substitute a different measure from the one asked.

The combined ratio including operating expenses needs premium, losses, loss-handling expenses and the company's operating (underwriting/administrative) expenses. The warehouse has no operating expense measure. The only expense data is claim-level: expense_payment and expense_reserve, which hold claim handling costs. The non-premium rows in policy_amount have no Amount_Type_Code and are not labeled, so they cannot be treated as operating expenses. Computing the ratio from claim amounts and premium alone would leave out the operating expenses the question asks to include.

The data has no smoke detector attribute. fire_claim holds only loss ratio, distance to the nearest fire station, number of firefighters, fireplace (yes/no) and year built, and no other table records smoke detectors or any property safety feature. Fireplace is a different measure and would not be a valid substitute.

No table or column in the database records square footage or any home size. fire_claim holds only loss ratio, nearest fire station distance, number of firefighters, fireplace and year built, and its identifying columns are empty. The claim, insurable_object and location tables also hold no property size or area attribute.

The data has no replacement cost value for the property at 5315 Martin Ave. That address maps to insurable object 1, which has only two kinds of policy amounts per coverage year. One is the annual premium, which is flagged in the premium table. The other is a constant 1,000,000 with an empty Amount_Type_Code and no label. The warehouse describes these rows as not labeled, so they could be a coverage limit, insured value or sum insured, and nothing shows they are replacement cost. Reporting 1,000,000 as the replacement cost value would substitute an unverified measure.

The data does not record the type of policy (home vs auto). Product_Identifier, Insurable_Object_Type_Code, Coverage_Part_Code, Coverage_Description and Insurance_Type_Code are all empty. The warehouse has only 2 policies, and every insured object is a property at an Austin address. Nothing distinguishes a home policy from an auto policy, so policyholders with both cannot be identified.

The warehouse has no reinsurance data. There is no reinsurer party or role (party roles are only AG, UW and PH, and the only organization is the insurer itself). There is also no ceded premium measure or cession or treaty table. Premium exists only as direct policy premium (policy_amount rows marked in premium), and as a fire_claim Premium column that is empty. Substituting direct premium would be a different measure from ceded premium.

The data holds neither date the question needs. Claim_Reported_Date is empty in every claim row (0 of 2 non-null), and claim_amount has no date of its own: Event_Date is empty, so a first payment cannot be dated. Claim_Open_Date is filled, but it is not the report date, and using it would substitute a different measure.

The data holds neither measure. There is no adjuster assignment event or date: party_role only has Agent, Underwriter and PolicyHolder, and no table links a party to a claim. First notice of loss is not recorded either, since claim.Claim_Reported_Date is empty. Claim_Open_Date is an open date, not a notice date, so using it would substitute a different measure.

The data has no adjuster information. The only party roles are Agent (AG), Underwriter (UW) and PolicyHolder (PH), and no table links a claim to a party. Claims connect only to policy coverage, occurrence, insurable object and catastrophe. Naming the agent, underwriter or policy holder would be a different measure from the adjuster.

The data has no county attribute. Addresses carry only street, city (Austin), state (TX), and postal code, and geographic_location has no county, name, or parent-region values. Premium is available by postal code (78732: 12,000; 78751: 86,000), but mapping zip codes to Travis County would rely on outside knowledge, not on anything the warehouse holds.

Loss ratio exists only in fire_claim.Loss_Ratio, and PolicyNo is NULL in all 820 rows (0 non-null, 0 distinct). The table has no other key and is not linked to the policy or claim tables, so the loss ratio cannot be grouped or averaged by policy number. Deriving a loss ratio from claim_amount and policy premiums would substitute a different measure, because no approved loss ratio metric exists there.

results.name: heldout-unanswerable-what-premium-did-each-fire-claim-s-policy-carry-8181b0

answer.sql: SELECT cl.Claim_Identifier, cl.Company_Claim_Number, pcd.Policy_Identifier, pa.Policy_Amount AS Premium FROM claim cl JOIN catastrophe c ON c.Catastrophe_Identifier = cl.Catastrophe_Identifier AND c.Catastrophe_Name = 'Fire' JOIN claim_coverage cc ON cc.Claim_Identifier = cl.Claim_Identifier JOIN policy_coverage_detail pcd ON pcd.Effective_Date = cc.Effective_Date AND pcd.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier = cc.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier LEFT JOIN policy_amount pa ON pa.Effective_Date = pcd.Effective_Date AND pa.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier = pcd.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier AND pa.Policy_Amount_Identifier IN (SELECT Policy_Amount_Identifier FROM premium) ORDER BY cl.Claim_Identifier

results.finalSql: SELECT cl.Claim_Identifier, cl.Company_Claim_Number, pcd.Policy_Identifier, pa.Policy_Amount AS Premium FROM claim cl JOIN catastrophe c ON c.Catastrophe_Identifier = cl.Catastrophe_Identifier AND c.Catastrophe_Name = 'Fire' JOIN claim_coverage cc ON cc.Claim_Identifier = cl.Claim_Identifier JOIN policy_coverage_detail pcd ON pcd.Effective_Date = cc.Effective_Date AND pcd.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier = cc.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier LEFT JOIN policy_amount pa ON pa.Effective_Date = pcd.Effective_Date AND pa.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier = pcd.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier AND pa.Policy_Amount_Identifier IN (SELECT Policy_Amount_Identifier FROM premium) ORDER BY cl.Claim_Identifier

answer.declineReason: No table or column records wind speed. The catastrophe table holds only a peril name such as 'Tornado', and occurrences has only dates and empty descriptive fields. Neither has any weather or wind measurement, so wind speed during a tornado cannot be determined from this data.

No table has an email address or phone number column. Person holds only names, party holds only identifiers, and location_address holds only postal address fields. The data cannot give a policyholder's email or phone.

The warehouse has no quote data. There is no quote table or quote status, and the agreement table holds only policies (its identifiers match policy.Policy_Identifier). Quotes that did not convert to policies cannot be identified or counted, and counting policies, assessments or claims would answer a different question.

No table or column holds a claims-made retroactive date for a policy. The policy table has only Effective_Date, Expiration_Date and Policy_Number. The claim table has Claims_Made_Date and Entry_Into_Claims_Made_Program_Date, but these belong to claims rather than policies, are not retroactive dates, and are empty in this data. Using the policy effective date or the agreement inception date instead would be a different measure.

The data has no home age or year built for the insured properties. The only Year_Built column is in fire_claim, a stand-alone sample of 820 fire-claim risk records. It has no policy, claim or location key (PolicyNo, ClaimNumber and InsuredLocation are empty), so it cannot be tied to the two policies. insurable_object holds only a location, with an empty object type, and has no construction year or age. Averaging fire_claim.Year_Built would describe a different population, not the homes insured under these policies.

answer.declineReason: The data has no way to identify legal defense costs. Expense payments (the expense_payment table joined to claim_amount) cover the cost of handling a claim in general, and I found no field that separates legal defense from other handling costs such as adjuster fees or inspections. Amount_Type_Code, Insurance_Type_Code and Claim_Offer_Identifier are empty for every expense payment, and the claim description is empty too. Reporting the expense payment total (3700 across 2 payments) would answer a different question, so I am not substituting it.

Market share needs our premium or policy volume divided by the total market in Austin, including competitors. This warehouse holds only our own data: the only organization is the insurer itself (MUSIC), and no table has competitor or industry-wide figures. Every location is already in Austin, so a share computed from this data would be 100% by construction and would not be a real market share.

The data does not record whether a claim was denied. Claim_Status_Code and Claim_Description are empty (NULL) for every claim, and no other table holds a claim outcome or denial indicator. The assessment_result table only holds underwriting results with the value 'OK', not claim outcomes.

The data holds addresses only for insured properties (insurable_object -> geographic_location -> location_address). No table links a party, person or policyholder to an address: party has only an identifier, person has only names, and agreement_party_role has only agreement, party and role columns. A policyholder's residence cannot be compared with the insured property's address.

The data holds no IBNR (incurred but not reported) reserve. The only reserves are case reserves on reported claims (loss_reserve and expense_reserve markers on claim_amount), and claim_amount has no usable date (Event_Date and Amount_Type_Code are empty). Claim reported dates are also empty. So neither IBNR nor a year-end 2019 reserve snapshot can be derived without substituting a different measure.

The data holds only the premium already charged for policy 31003000337: 12,000 (annual) for the term 2019-06-01 to 2020-05-31. It has no renewal quote, future-term premium, rate change or pricing model. Reporting the current premium as the renewal premium would substitute a different measure.

The warehouse has no occupation attribute for the insured. The person table holds only names, plus empty birth date and gender columns. The party table has no occupation field, and organizations holds only the insurer itself. Policy 31003000336 can be linked to its policy holder, but that holder's occupation is not recorded anywhere.

The data has no employee count or employee/headcount attribute. The organizations table holds only the insurer itself (Mesa Underwriters Specialty Insurance Company) with identifier, name, industry and type columns, none of which record employees. The person table covers policy holders, agents and underwriters, and nothing marks a person as an employee of the company, so counting persons would substitute a different measure.

The data has no cause-of-loss field of the kind the question describes (electrical, cooking, etc.). Claim 12312702 (Claim_Identifier 2) links only to catastrophe 'Fire', which is a broad peril type, not a cause. Claim_Description and Occurrence_Name are empty, and no other table records a cause of loss.

The data does not record which coverages a policy includes. In policy_coverage_detail, Coverage_Identifier, Coverage_Part_Code, Coverage_Description and Coverage_Inclusion_Exclusion_Code are NULL in all 6 rows, and no other table has a coverage type column. 'Flood' appears only as a peril name in catastrophe, which describes claims that occurred, not coverage a policy includes. Counting policies with flood claims would answer a different question.

The warehouse has no discount data. For policy 31003000337 there are only two policy_amount rows: a 12,000 annual premium (Amount_Type_Code 'Year', listed in premium) and an unlabeled 600,000 amount that is not a premium. No table or column records discounts, so the discounts applied to the premium cannot be determined.

Claim 12312701 is the company claim number of claim 1, and it has one loss payment (Claim_Amount_Identifier 3, amount 1200). The payment has no date in the data. claim_amount.Event_Date is NULL for that row, and the model documents Event_Date as empty for every amount, so an amount has no date of its own. The claim's open and close dates and the occurrence date describe the claim and the loss, not the payment, so using one of them would answer a different question.

The data has no field that records a total loss or a destroyed home. fire_claim only holds risk attributes (Loss_Ratio, fire station distance, firefighters, fireplace, year built), and Loss_Ratio is a ratio, not a total-loss flag. PolicyNo and ClaimNumber are empty in every fire_claim row, so its records cannot be identified or joined to claims. The claim, catastrophe and claim_amount tables can mark a Fire catastrophe and hold amounts, but none indicates a total loss or destruction of the home.

The data has no record of installment payments made by a policyholder. The only money tied to policy 31003000337 is an annual premium of 12000 (Amount_Type_Code 'Year') and an unlabeled amount of 600000. Neither shows what was paid, in installments or otherwise, and no table holds payment transactions, installment schedules or payment dates. The claim payment tables (loss_payment, expense_payment) cover claim payouts, not premium installments the policyholder paid.

The data has no fire department response time. The fire_claim table only records Nearest_Firestation_miles (a distance), Number_of_Firefighters, Loss_Ratio, Fireplace and Year_Built. The claim and occurrence tables have open and close dates and occurrence begin and end dates, but nothing that records when the fire department was dispatched or arrived. Distance to the nearest fire station is not a response time, and the claim settlement time is a different measure.

Nothing in the data records whether a claim was litigated. The claim table has no litigation flag, and its status code and description columns are empty. The claim_amount subtypes cover only loss and expense payments and reserves, so legal expense cannot be identified. The catastrophe names are only peril types, and the other tables hold no legal-action information.

The data has no sales-channel attribute, so online sales cannot be told apart from agent sales. The only distribution information is agreement_party_role, where every policy has an agent (AG) and a policy holder (PH). The party_role code list contains only AG, UW and PH, and the only organization is the insurer itself. No policy is marked as sold online, so there is no online group to compare with agents. The fire_claim table has a Loss_Ratio column, but it is not linked to policies or agents.
